messages.text: I might choose {product}.
Do you want me to add it to the comparison?
Correction: the word might in my earlier message was inaccurate; I had already chosen {product} on {date_from}.
Should I save the selection confirmation?
Save it with the setup fee estimate.
The confirmation is saved with the estimate.

expected.claim: The user corrects earlier wording: the user had already chosen {product} on {date_from}.
expected.quote: Correction: the word might in my earlier message was inaccurate; I had already chosen {product} on {date_from}.

messages.text: I sent {person} an update about {product}.
Do you want me to open the update?
Correction to my earlier update: I had not approved the {product} plan; I had only asked for its price.
Should I attach the estimate to the budget draft?
Yes, attach it to the current draft.
The estimate is attached.

expected.claim: The user corrects the earlier update: the user had only asked for the {product} price and had not approved the plan.
expected.quote: Correction to my earlier update: I had not approved the {product} plan; I had only asked for its price.

messages.text: The note from yesterday was about the {product} trial.
Do you want me to reopen the note?
Correction to that note: I did not reject {product}; I paused the trial while comparing its renewal price.
Should I leave the reminder active?
Yes, leave the reminder for Friday.
The reminder is active.

expected.claim: The user corrects the note: the user paused the {product} trial while comparing its renewal price and did not reject it.
expected.quote: Correction to that note: I did not reject {product}; I paused the trial while comparing its renewal price.

messages.text: I wrote that I was considering {product}.
Would you like the note changed?
Correction: I had already chosen {product} on {date_from}; the earlier phrase about considering it was inaccurate.
Should I attach the selection confirmation?
Yes, put it with the comparison.
The confirmation is attached.

expected.claim: The user corrects earlier wording: the user had already chosen {product} on {date_from}.
expected.quote: Correction: I had already chosen {product} on {date_from}; the earlier phrase about considering it was inaccurate.

messages.text: I told {person} I was done with {product}.
Do you mean the review or the subscription?
To clarify my earlier wording, I had finished reviewing {product}'s terms; I did not mean that I had ended the subscription.
Would you like the renewal notice forwarded?
Yes, send it to the shared inbox.
The notice was forwarded.

expected.claim: The user clarifies that the earlier phrase done referred to finishing review of {product}'s terms, not to ending the subscription.
expected.quote: To clarify my earlier wording, I had finished reviewing {product}'s terms; I did not mean that I had ended the subscription.

messages.text: The meeting summary mentions {product} billing.
Should I open the summary?
Correction to the summary: I had not switched to annual billing; I had only requested the annual price quote for {product}.
Should I request the monthly quote too?
Yes, ask for both billing options.
The request is sent.

expected.claim: The user corrects the summary: the user had only requested {product}'s annual price quote and had not switched to annual billing.
expected.quote: Correction to the summary: I had not switched to annual billing; I had only requested the annual price quote for {product}.

messages.text: I chose monthly billing for {product} on {date_from}, then changed that decision and chose its annual plan on {date_to}.
Should I save the updated confirmation?
Yes, archive the annual confirmation.
Archive status: saved.
Keep the earlier confirmation next to it.
Both confirmations are saved together.

expected.claim: The user chose monthly billing for {product} on {date_from}.
expected.quote: I chose monthly billing for {product} on {date_from}, then changed that decision and chose its annual plan on {date_to}.

expected.claim: The user changed that decision and chose the annual plan for {product} on {date_to}.
expected.quote: changed that decision and chose its annual plan on {date_to}

messages.text: I committed to the annual {product} plan on {date_from}; on {date_to}, I reversed that decision and switched to monthly billing instead.
Would you like the old invoice copied to the renewal folder?
Yes, keep both invoices together.
The folder now contains both invoices.

expected.claim: The user committed to the annual {product} plan on {date_from}.
expected.quote: I committed to the annual {product} plan on {date_from}; on {date_to}, I reversed that decision and switched to monthly billing instead.

expected.claim: The user reversed that decision and switched to monthly billing on {date_to}.
expected.quote: on {date_to}, I reversed that decision and switched to monthly billing instead.

messages.text: I tried to upload the {object} scan to {product} on {date_from}, but the transfer failed before the file arrived.
Would a new upload link help?
Yes, send it to the same address.

expected.claim: The user's attempt to upload a scan of the {object} to {product} failed before the file arrived on {date_from}.
expected.quote: I tried to upload the {object} scan to {product} on {date_from}, but the transfer failed before the file arrived.

messages.text: I am considering renewing {product} on {date_from}, but I have not chosen a plan or submitted payment.
The renewal page has monthly and annual options. Should I compare the prices?
Show me the monthly rate first.
Preview panel opened for monthly pricing.

expected.claim: The user is considering renewing {product} on {date_from}, but has not chosen a plan or submitted payment.
expected.quote: I am considering renewing {product} on {date_from}, but I have not chosen a plan or submitted payment.

messages.text: Did I choose {product} on {date_from}, or was I still comparing options?
I can search the decision log if you want.
If I had chosen {product} on {date_from}, would the order have processed?
Would you like an explanation of the checkout flow?
Please explain the steps.
The meeting notes say {person} nominated me to coordinate the {object}; I have not accepted the role.
Should I add a tentative entry to the agenda?
Leave the agenda unchanged until the minutes are approved.
I left the draft as it is.
Add a reminder to revisit the nomination after the next meeting.
I added the reminder to the agenda draft.

expected.claim: The user reports that the meeting notes say {person} nominated the user to coordinate the {object}; the user has not accepted the role.
expected.quote: The meeting notes say {person} nominated me to coordinate the {object}; I have not accepted the role.

messages.text: I own the {object}; {person} is repairing it and has the item until {date_to}.
Do you need a reminder near the pickup date?
Yes, put one on my calendar.
The reminder is set for the return date.

expected.claim: The user owns the {object}; {person} is repairing it and has the item until {date_to}.
expected.quote: I own the {object}; {person} is repairing it and has the item until {date_to}

messages.text: The invoice lists {person} as owner of the {object}; I paid the invoice on behalf of our team.
Should I attach the receipt to the team folder?
Yes, file it under shared equipment.

expected.claim: The user reports that the invoice lists {person} as owner of the {object}; the user paid the invoice for the team.
expected.quote: The invoice lists {person} as owner of the {object}; I paid the invoice on behalf of our team.

messages.text: My signed registration lists me as owner of the {object} from {date_from}; {person} keeps the item at {place}.
Should I include the storage location in the inventory?
Yes, put it beside the registration date.
The inventory entry is updated.

expected.claim: The user's signed registration lists the user as owner of the {object} from {date_from}; {person} keeps the item at {place}.
expected.quote: My signed registration lists me as owner of the {object} from {date_from}; {person} keeps the item at {place}.

messages.text: The roster names me as reviewer for {product} and {person} as approver; I can comment, but I cannot approve.
Should I send the review link to both of you?
Send it to {person} and copy me.
The link is ready.

expected.claim: The user reports that the roster names the user as reviewer for {product} and {person} as approver; the user can comment but cannot approve.
expected.quote: The roster names me as reviewer for {product} and {person} as approver; I can comment, but I cannot approve.

messages.text: I own the {object}; {person} is storing it for me at {place}.
Would you like the storage receipt attached to the inventory?
Yes, attach the receipt.
The receipt is attached.

expected.claim: The user owns the {object}; {person} stores the item for the user at {place}.
expected.quote: I own the {object}; {person} is storing it for me at {place}.

messages.text: I administer {product} for the committee, but the committee owns the account and I cannot transfer it.
Would you like the billing history opened?
Open billing history only.
Billing history is open.
Export the last three invoices to the folder.
The export is ready in the folder.

expected.claim: The user administers {product} for the committee; the committee owns the account, and the user cannot transfer it.
expected.quote: I administer {product} for the committee, but the committee owns the account and I cannot transfer it.

messages.text: I lent my {object} to {person} on {date_from}; {person} has the item now, but it is still mine.
Should I add a return reminder?
Not yet; add the loan date to the inventory.
I updated the inventory.

expected.claim: The user lent the {object} to {person} on {date_from}; {person} currently has the item, and the user says the item remains the user's property.
expected.quote: I lent my {object} to {person} on {date_from}; {person} has the item now, but it is still mine.

messages.text: The committee voted to retain {product}; I recorded the vote, but I did not decide alone.
Should I file the minutes with the project documents?
Yes, file them under governance.
The minutes are filed.

expected.claim: The user reports that the committee voted to retain {product}; the user recorded the vote and did not decide alone.
expected.quote: The committee voted to retain {product}; I recorded the vote, but I did not decide alone.

messages.text: I am storing {person}'s {object} at {place}; {person} owns it, and I am responsible only for keeping it safe.
Would an inventory label help?
Yes, put it on the outside of the case.
The label is ready.

expected.claim: The user has custody of the {object} at {place}; {person} owns it, and the user is responsible only for keeping it safe.
expected.quote: I am storing {person}'s {object} at {place}; {person} owns it, and I am responsible only for keeping it safe.

messages.text: Is {person} the owner of the {object}, or only the custodian?
I can check the inventory record if you want.
If I stored the {object} for {person}, would I become its owner?
Would you like a general explanation of custody?
Please explain the general rule.
